detail.title: Synthesis of Observer Disagreement Mechanisms
detail.summary: We synthesize findings regarding observer disagreement and variance in empirical research. Reviewing the available evidence from scholarly sources, we find that observer disagreement often stems not merely from 'bias' or 'error' in the classical sense, but from structural differences in predictive model calibration, historical geographical context, and the framing of insurgency and inequality data. This project clarifies the distinction between disagreement arising from raw data interpretation versus disagreement arising from the underlying conceptual frameworks employed by the observer. We have mapped these differences into an initial framework for observer variance, emphasizing that 'disagreement' functions as a signal of model-mismatch or context-dependency rather than simple inaccuracy. Future research will deepen the investigation into predictive model alignment.
